objetivo: For students to recognize the characteristics of living things (they are born, grow, feed, reproduce, and die) and classify them into the major kingdoms: animal, plant, fungi, and microorganisms.
hatsumon: What do a dog, a tree, and you have in common?

turnos.utterance_formal: Today we're going to bring some order to nature: we're going to study living things.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Today we're going to bring some order to nature: we're going to study living things.

turnos.utterance_formal: Take out your notebooks, because today we're going to make several lists and classifications.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Take out your notebooks, because today we're going to make several lists and classifications.

turnos.utterance_formal: Think about something: what do a dog, a tree, and you yourselves have in common?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay, think about it: what do a dog, a tree, and you yourselves have in common?

turnos.utterance_formal: They seem very different, right? A dog runs and a tree doesn't even move.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: They look pretty different, right? A dog runs and a tree doesn't even move.

turnos.utterance_formal: In nature there are things that have life and things that don't.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: In nature there are things that have life and things that don't.

operations.text: There are things with **life** and things without life.

turnos.utterance_formal: The ones that have life we call living things: everything that is born, grows, and dies.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The ones that have life we call living things: everything that is born, grows, and dies.

set.text: There are things with **life** and things without life. Living things are everything that is born, grows, and dies.

turnos.utterance_formal: Sounds simple, but there's more detail to it. Let's look at it closely.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Sounds simple, but there's more to it. Let's look at it closely.

turnos.utterance_formal: Every living thing does five things throughout its life: it is born, grows, feeds, reproduces and dies.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Every living thing does five little things throughout its life: it's born, grows, feeds, reproduces and dies.

operations.text:
Is born
Grows
Feeds
Reproduces
Dies

turnos.utterance_formal: Notice that a dog, a tree, and you all meet all five: that's why all three are alive.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Notice that a dog, a tree, and you all meet all five: that's why all three are alive.

operations.text: Every living thing does all five.

turnos.utterance_formal: Reproducing means having children or offspring, so life can go on.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Re producing means having children or offspring, so life can go on.

set.text: Every living thing does all five. Reproducing means having offspring, so life can go on.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now let's compare them to things without life. A rock, for example, doesn't get born or grow.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now let's compare them to things without life. A rock, for example, doesn't get born or grow.

operations.text: A rock isn't born and doesn't grow, so it has no **life**

turnos.utterance_formal: A dog, on the other hand, does: it's born, eats, grows, and has offspring.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: A dog, on the other hand, does: it's born, eats, grows, and has offspring.

set.text: A rock isn't born and doesn't grow, so it has no **life**. A dog, on the other hand, is born, eats, grows, and has offspring.

turnos.utterance_formal: Can you see the difference? That's the important part.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Did you catch the difference? That's the important part.

turnos.utterance_formal: Let's remember what a living thing is and what it does.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Let's remember what a living thing is and what it does.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now then, living things are extremely numerous and varied, so we group them into kingdoms.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now then, living things are a ton and super varied, so we group them into kingdoms.

turnos.utterance_formal: A kingdom is a large group of living things that are similar to each other. Let's start with the first one.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: A kingdom is a large group of living things that are similar to each other. Let's start with the first one.

set.text: Living things are grouped into **kingdoms**, large groups of similar living things.

turnos.utterance_formal: The animal kingdom: these are the ones that move on their own and eat other living things.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The animal kingdom: these are the ones that move on their own and eat other living things.

set.text: Living things are grouped into **kingdoms**, large groups of similar living things. **Animals** move on their own and eat other living things.

turnos.utterance_formal: For example: the dog, the eagle, the fish, and the ant. Make a list.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: For example: the dog, the eagle, the fish, and the a nt. Make me a little list.

turnos.utterance_formal: And to help us remember, here's an example dog.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And to help us remember, here's a little example dog.

turnos.utterance_formal: We, human beings, are also part of the animal kingdom.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: We, human beings, are also part of the animal kingdom, you know.

turnos.utterance_formal: The second one is the plant kingdom: they make their own food and don't move from their spot.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The second one is the plant kingdom: they make their own food and don't move from their spot.

operations.text: Plants make their own **food** and don't move.

turnos.utterance_formal: For example: the tree, the rose, grass, and the fern. Another list.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: For example: the tree, the rose, grass, and the fern. Another little list.

turnos.utterance_formal: And an example of this is a plant.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And an example of this is a little plant.

turnos.utterance_formal: Did you all copy down the first two kingdoms? Very good.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Did you all copy down the first two kingdoms?… alright, very good.

turnos.utterance_formal: Let's remember: we have the animal kingdom and the plant kingdom.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Let's remember: we've got the animal kingdom and the plant kingdom.

turnos.utterance_formal: The third one surprises a lot of people: the fungi kingdom. They're not plants or animals.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The third one surprises a lot of people: the fungi kingdom. They're not plants or animals.

turnos.utterance_formal: For example: mushrooms, bread mold, and yeast. Your list.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: For example: mush rooms, bread mold, and ye ast. Your little list.

turnos.utterance_formal: Did you know the green mold on bread is a fungus? Yep.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Did you know the green mold on bread is a fungus? Yep, it is.

turnos.utterance_formal: And there's one more kingdom with the smallest living things of all: microorganisms.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And there's one more kingdom with the smallest living things of all: micro organisms.

operations.text: Microorganisms are so small you can't see them without a **microscope**.

turnos.utterance_formal: This includes bacteria and other microbes that live everywhere.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: This includes bac teria and other microbes that live everywhere.

turnos.utterance_formal: Even though we don't see them, they're even on our hands. That's why we wash them.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Even though we don't see them, they're even on our hands. That's why we wash them.

operations.text: Microbes are even on our hands, and that is why we wash them.

turnos.utterance_formal: Some microbes help us and others cause diseases.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Some microbes help us and others cause diseases.

set.text: Microbes are even on our hands, and that is why we wash them. Some microbes help us, others cause **diseases**.

turnos.utterance_formal: Notice the four kingdoms we have written down.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Notice the four kingdoms we've got written down.

turnos.utterance_formal: Do you have all four? Perfect, let's start wrapping up.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Do you have all four yet? Perfect, let's start wrapping up.

turnos.utterance_formal: So there are four big kingdoms of living things, clearly.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So there are four big kingdoms of living things, nice and clear.

operations.text: There are four big kingdoms of living things.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now think: what's the point of going through the trouble of classifying them?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now think: what's the point of going through the trouble of classi fying them?

set.text: There are four big kingdoms of living things. Grouping them helps us study and **protect** them.

turnos.utterance_formal: And all of them, from the biggest to the smallest, are important for nature.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And all of them, from the biggest to the tiniest, are important for nature.

set.text: There are four big kingdoms of living things. Grouping them helps us study and **protect** them. All of them are important for nature.

turnos.utterance_formal: Let's remember why we classify them: to study and protect them better.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Let's remember why we classify them: to study and protect them better.

turnos.utterance_formal: Rest your hand for a moment. Are we good? Very good.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Give your hand a little rest. Are we good?… alright, very good.

turnos.utterance_formal: So you don't forget, hold on to the two big ideas from today.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So you don't forget, hold on to the two big ideas from today.

operations.text: A living thing is born, grows, feeds, reproduces, and dies.

turnos.utterance_formal: And the second one: living things are grouped into animal, plant, fungi, and microbes.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And the second one: living things are grouped into animal, plant, fungi, and microbes.

set.text: A living thing is born, grows, feeds, reproduces, and dies. Living things are grouped into animal, plant, fungi, and microbe kingdoms.

turnos.utterance_formal: And today's big word, the one you shouldn't forget, is kingdom.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And today's big word, the one you shouldn't forget, is kingdom.

set.text: A living thing is born, grows, feeds, reproduces, and dies. Living things are grouped into animal, plant, fungi, and microbe kingdoms. The key word is **kingdom**.

turnos.utterance_formal: Remember what a living thing is: everything that is born, grows, and dies.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Remember what a living thing is: everything that is born, grows, and dies.

turnos.utterance_formal: Very good, I can see it's clear. Excellent work.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Very good, I can see it's super clear. Excellent work, everyone.

turnos.utterance_formal: For homework, choose five living things and say which kingdom each one belongs to.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: For homework, choose five living things and say which kingdom each one goes in.

operations.text: Classify five living things into their kingdom.

turnos.utterance_formal: And explain to me, in your own words, what makes a living thing alive.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And explain to me, in your own words, what makes a living thing alive.

set.text: Classify five living things into their kingdom. Explain what makes a living thing alive.

turnos.utterance_formal: And with that we answered the question we started the class with.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And with that we already answered the question we kicked off the class with.

turnos.utterance_formal: They all do the same five things: a dog, a tree, and you are born, grow, feed, reproduce, and die.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: They all do the same five things, see: a dog, a tree, and you, all born, grow, feed, reproduce, and die.

operations.text: A dog, a tree, and you are all born, grow, feed, reproduce, and die.

turnos.utterance_formal: That's all for today. Pack up your things and see you tomorrow.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's all for today. Pack up your things and see you tomorrow, take care.
